html:
Who He Is

Hugo Doris Marta, Baron Darryl, was descended from Pramaterie Leonora, the eleventh in a row, and owned a small estate on the outskirts of the huge Labelin: a dozen villages and a couple of thousand acres of arable land. Influence and weight gave him the patronage of Duke Maurice Labelin, whose trusted vassal and military leader he was. He was followed by the glory of a cruel and gloomy man. Merchant Harmon, having received from Count Vittor Shayland a list of possible buyers of the Light Sphere, went to Darryl in the second place precisely because the baron scared him “to hell”. (Radiant Sphere) In Moger Buckley's mind, he was "the iron fist of the master", Harmon called him "the chain beast of the Labelins", and Duke Aiden Almera called him "the chain dog of the Labelin".

Appearance and temper

Harmon saw the Baron wearing a white shirt and a black camsol. The thin lips were bent downwards, the eyes deeply planted, the eyebrows fused on the nose, and it seemed that the feeling of joy to the baron was “long forgotten, or even not known at all.” His voice was low and hard. He knew how to instantly switch from a roar to a cold half-whistle and always said to the merchant “you”, which sounded especially creepy. Even his laughter did not touch his face: “Ha-ha-ha” was torn out of his mouth, and there was no smile.

Baron's cruelty was commonplace. At Harmon, the maid spilled tea, and Darryl lazily pressed her palm against the table with a metal kettle. In the courtyard of his castle stood crosses of crossed logs, and on one hung a braided guy who hung there clearly not the first day. Buckley heard how the men who had been guilty before the baron came to an end: one was tore by four horses, the other was sharded until ribs appeared from under the meat. For the foolish mistake of the servants, Darryl offered Harmon “twenty lashes each.”

Darryl Castle

The castle stood on a hill above the surrounding villages. On the one hand, the hill was steeper, the other slope went into a swampy lowland. The road looped between the ponds and the tops. The garden on the slope was abandoned: the lawns were overgrown with weed, the statues had their hands and noses beaten off. But the strip of cutting around the walls was cleaned to the last bush. The yard was arranged "according to all the rules of military science": a smooth platform was shot from the corner towers, the buildings were pressed against the walls, the doors were chained with iron and covered with granite blocks from the ram, the roofs were covered with tiles from fire arrows. The Baron's luminary, with two narrow windows-warriors to the north and dark portraits of ancestors, was almost without light. Joaquin called the castle a "good fortress", and Harmon, looking at the crosses, regretted that he had not yielded to the Gobart-Synthal Sphere. (Gobart-Sintal)

Deal with the Light Sphere

In June 1774, Harmon waited four days for an answer to the letter, and then was taken for tea in the presence of the Baroness: the Baron, according to him, had no secrets from his wife. The Baroness, a yellow-skinned lady in a gray dress and cap, who looked like a ferret, called the merchant a madman and a fraud and advised him to send him "to the cross". Darryl did not waste time on courtesy: “I too have a little honor to talk to the merchant.” Harmon listed a price of forty-one thousand ephes. The Baron immediately realized that it can only be about the Sacred Object, and demanded the name of the owner. The merchant said only that behind him was one of the great lords-landlords, who would come to return his "with all his might" if the goods were taken away. Harmon added that he knows how much the Duke bought the former Item, and that the new one is five thousand more expensive, because "is capable of some wonderful interaction with the owner." The Baron promised to send a letter when the Duke could inspect the goods.

On June 27, the baron sat to the right of the duke at a meeting in Labelin and reprimanded the merchant for being late: the duke had to make three hundred miles by train from the capital because of him. Harmon explained that he had spent twelve days in captivity. Darryl said it was his own fault, since he was stingy with the guards. When examining the fake, the Duke noticed an axis at the inner ring, and Darryl, looking at the description from the register, decided that the ring should hang in the air, and remembered the "Eternal Flow" item in the Cathedral of Agatha the Radiant in the First Winter, where the light hangs inside the hoop by itself. The Duke waved back, “This first winter has gone dark! “What have you forgotten, Lord?” Darryl then wrote out a bill in the bank for 36,000 ephemera in the name of Harmon, sealed it with the coat of arms of the Labelins and said goodbye to the merchant:

“You disgust me, as does your master. You embody all the abomination that is inherent in the class of merchants: cowardice, cunning, pettiness, complete lack of dignity and honor. ”

For details on the transaction, see Sale of the Light Sphere. (Sale of the Radiant Sphere) Harmon initially suspected that the kidnapping was arranged by the baron himself or by one of his associates: only Darryl and his closest servants knew about the Object in Labelin. Then he decided that the monks-the kidnappers have a spy in the Baron's castle.

War with Origen

In the autumn of 1774, in the Northern War, Darryl took all the cavalry of the Southern Way from under Labelin to the army of General Silver Fox. (Alexis Smile) In early December 1774, at the Battle of Pixie, Lis sent her, reinforced by the scarlet guard, to one of the flanks, and the North repulsed the attack. In the same battle, the Baron's sword pierced Donald Northwood, who was trying to save his brother, and crushed his jaw. Later, Magda Labelin cruelly reminded the Baron that his knights surrendered to Origin at the Wise River and at Windley and fled from him at Labelin. Buckley in his thoughts called the Baron famous in three fights: in one he "stretched his sides to the bears of Northwood", and of the other two he "extremely successfully ran".

“The Useful People”

In January 1775, at Grace, Darryl proposed to Maurice Labelin to attack. According to his calculations, the northerners held only two companies in Doyle, Windley, Soltown and Elfort and a battalion in Labelin, and the Labelins had four thousand horsemen. Lady Magda ridiculed his plans and "failure as a general", and the Duke announced that he would no longer fight with Origin, but would buy. When Buckley spoke of the 50,000 spark eyes that the Shimmerians sell, the Baron exclaimed that it was more than the Silver Fox had at Pixie. The Duke sent his daughter to Shimmery with two million gold, and with her Darryl "with a whole regiment" and Buckley. He told Magda to speak to the southerners, because the Soldafons have “oak tongues”.

Shimmering campaign

A fleet of Labelins led by the flagship "Great" sailed from under Grace to the south and in March 1775 came to Laam; (Laem) Buckley and four underlings outscored the squadron by three days on the dog-on-the-barrel corvette. On a six-week voyage, the baron reminded Buckley that the low-born must know his place: he knocked out his tooth and threw him overboard, but Buckley picked up the next ship. In Laem, Darryl demanded that Buckley find Harmon, because he was deceived, not by Magda, but by himself: "This bastard did not deceive Lady Magda, but me." Then he said, “What an honor. Get out."

Negotiations to buy eyes have failed. For five days, the Shimmerian nobles fed the travelers with flattery, gifts, wine and spectacles, and Magda and Darryl unsuccessfully tried to reduce the conversation to their eyes; four of the Five flatly refused to sell them. The baron then told the soldiers to shut the mouths of the musicians and dancers so that Magda could give her famous speech. In the new round, he chastised hired General Lorinal Gitan as a "servant not of honor, but of coins" and listened with a sagging jaw to Prince Hector's "conciliatory gift": a score of nine and a half thousand ephesas for hospitality. (Hector of Shimmery) Admitting defeat, he was the first to say out loud, "I'm afraid, my lady, we will have to admit defeat." Then Magda, instead of going back to her father, asked what he, the Baron, really wanted. Darryl found in himself the only desire and "blinked with the grin of a wolf." His knights became the force with which Magda captured the Shimmerian caravan with eyes. Before the battle, Darryl raised a special banner on the Great mast: two Buckley's henchmen, still alive, suspended on hooks under the ribs. Magda admitted, "Baron knows how to scare." Looking at the chests with eyes, the Baron said they would arm the two regiments and become "the first spark army in the service of the Great House".

After the landing, Darryl, on Magda's orders, sent couriers to the commanders of the mercenary brigades, promising a double fee. In May 1775, he entered the city of Iserin with the announcement: "Baron Hugo Darryl, warlord of the Great House of Labelins. From now on, the city of Iserin is under our control." Meanwhile, at Faunterra, the Duke of Maurice announced from the podium of the House that the South Road Expeditionary Corps, under the command of Baron Hugo Darryl, had begun fighting against Shimmery; Prince Hector threw the Duke a glove in response. At the end of May 1775, his knights broke into the Abode of Bezdna, where the Hunter's men had already captured the Second of the Five. Seeing the Hunter's face, the Baron tore off the helmet and coughed: "Lord Adrian?"..

Under Adrian

Upon meeting him in Harmon's Abode, Darryl immediately beat him with a patchwork glove, demanding to know where the Sphere was, and stopped only when Adrian appeared. The emperor declared the merchant his cupbearer, but the baron did not tire of burning his eyes at the table. The cook, a retired knight, idolized Darryl and therefore bullied Harmon. At the military councils, the baron offered to send an encrypted letter to the seigneur, so that Maurice Labelin would prepare troops for Adrian, who would be waiting in Gracende: "Every honest knight of the Southern Way will gladly draw a sword in the name of your victory!" At the beginning of June Adrian's army moved through the Lion Mountains and for three days descended to White Stone Bay; the baron fiercely maintained discipline among the travelers, and soldiers for scuffles. At the bay, when the rumors launched by Harmon led to a quarrel of travelers, mercenaries and Shavans, he demanded that Adrian refute the rumor that he was going to abolish the knighthood: "this vile gossip undermines the morale." From there, the Labelin squadron, bypassing the Surlion, delivered the army to the Southern Way.

In July 1775 in Grace, where Adrian married Magda, the baron met Harmon at the palace and announced to him that Duke Maurice had decided to leave the Light Sphere to the lord as a wedding gift and pardoned the merchant. He immediately beat Harmon with his fists and boots: “Nothing is settled. You tricked me. Shame on the Lord.” Adrian sent Darryl along with Count Quindar as ambassadors to Faunterra and promised to warn him to treat Harmon with care. The Baron's instruction was forgotten, barely leaving Grace. He forced the merchant to carry things, clean shoes and wash the bottom. In the inn near the station near Labelin, he reasoned with the knights that the liberator soldiers (former Salem people) passing by were suitable as "infantry meat", in which Minerva's kairs would get bogged down. There, at his table, it was said that “women can be useful”: Valerie Gracend, much indebted to the Duke of Maurice, had already sent a secret message to turn the Silver Fox swords in the right direction. (Valerie Graysend) In the Jack and Jane Inn, Harmon watered the ambassadors with a sleeping potion and took train tickets from the sleeping baron (see Harmon Paula Roger).

In August 1775, when Adrian's regiments, under the guise of a wedding celebration, entered Faunterra without a fight, the baron with sire Peter and two horses from the Lord's Guard reappeared in his teahouse, entering after Lady in Darkness and the Second of Five; Harmon was no longer with them. Magda greeted him with a rebuke: "Have you thought of changing your suzerainty?" At the reception at the palace, the clown Manson shook hands with a serious mine to every traveler from Maurice’s entourage (“Congratulations on the son-in-law... Slyly climbed"), and the baron pushed him away; when Ganta Birai put a jester knife to his stomach, Darryl bred them: "Ganta, this is a Manson jester. He loved the Lord, but he loved the Lord. At the end of September Maurice Labelin did not give his daughter to bodyguards ("I need him"), but the best knights of Darryl, tested in the Shimmerian campaign, made up her personal guard. When in the "liberation campaign" on the Labelin Adrian asked his wife what tricks to expect from the Origins, Magda flashed an answer. The cards were actually studied by the baron, and she only memorized his conclusions by heart. When Francis-Ilianus demanded to punish the commander of the Solar Regiment, she reminded Adrian that three people had “pulled him out”: herself, Baron Darryl and Colonel Horey. Before the Battle of the First Winter, Maurice and the Baron wanted to just wait for Shayland to crush the Origins. (Battle for First Winter) On December 2, the day of the battle, Darryl was in Main among the guests at the common table, where kings, lord and Lady in the Dark gathered. When Adrian lost his trump card after the battle, Magda threatened her husband that her father was sitting "at the headquarters of Baron Darryl", and the Labelin regiments were ready for battle and would unite with the Kairs.

In "Fantasies"

In Fantasias, which describe a possible future, Maurice and Magda Labelin live in the Venerable Citadel of Faunterra in the spring of 1776. The upper floors they filled with luxury, and the lower - the knights of Baron Hugo.

In the story "Ad-ri-an!" (November 1776), during the election of the lord, Erwin blamed Adrian in the House, and General Gore reported that Baron Darryl had been alerted and would call in troops from the South Road. At Adrian's council of war, where Horton's cuirres approached the capital, the baron reported that he had two hundred and forty knights in the Table Citadel, and that three hundred more swords would come from Labelin tomorrow and the day after. But he immediately made it clear that he had a direct order from the Duke of Maurice to protect the Holy Citadel and personally Lady Magda and in no case to engage in battle against the Kairs, because they are going "to your city, Lord." Shavan Zlataya Griva appreciated his audacity: “The guy with the eggs.” (Golden Mane) Adrian entrusted him with the protection of both palaces and threatened that the baron would not be pleased if even a hair fell from his son's head. Maurice Labelin himself, meanwhile, said in the House of Erwin: "I told Baron Darryl to guard Magda and not to help Adrian. I pray to the gods that he will carry out his orders.”

Trivia

  • In Arrow, Coin, Spark, Mira, posing as Lady Gloria Northwood, bargained with Duke Aiden Almera and remained silent with a meaningful smile when he asked if Hugo Darryl was not "her mother's man" surrounded by Labelin. Aiden doubted: “Baron is Labelin’s chain dog! Do you serve two masters?” The world in this conversation clearly bluffed, and the texts do not give confirmation.
  • Harmon believed that of all the assassins he knew, only Baron Darryl could be next to the Adrien Hunter.
